The [Distance Between Two Points Calculator](/distance-formula-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Find the straight-line distance between two coordinate points. Enter your x₁, y₁, x₂ and y₂ and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Find the straight-line distance between two coordinate points. This free online distance between two points calculator gives you an instant answer without an account, a download or sending your entries to a server. It is designed for quick everyday use on desktop and mobile. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Distance Between Two Points Calculator

Start by entering your x₁, then entering your y₁, entering your x₂ and finally entering your y₂. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your x₁.
2. Enter your y₁.
3. Enter your x₂.
4. Enter your y₂.
5. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
6. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

d = √((x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²).

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Distance Between Two Points Calculator](/distance-formula-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. The distance from (1,2) to (5,10) is √80 ≈ 8.9443. Try the same figures in the [Distance Between Two Points Calculator](/distance-formula-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

With the default values (x₁: 1, y₁: 2, x₂: 5, y₂: 10), the [Distance Between Two Points Calculator](/distance-formula-calculator) returns Distance: 8.94427191.
